items.title: When Justice ‘Lags’
items.description: How video testimony fails defendants, and the technology that could help fix it. A visual contrast between the flat, pixelated representation of current court video feeds and the immersive promise of future holographic testimony. (Image generated via AI) Picture the following scene: A woman sits in a detention center video room somewhere in the Southwest. A government-provided webcam is pointed at her face. On a screen across the room, and hundreds of miles away, an immigration judge looks back from a federal courtroom. She’s explaining why she fled her country. She says men came to her home.

items.title: The Death of Privacy in the “Always-On” Future
items.description: “Analprints” are real. So is the Fourth Amendment. They haven’t met yet. A visualization of a connected smart home, where data from the resident and various devices streams upward to the cloud. (Image generated via AI) The Frictionless Morning She has said no words aloud. Her eyes are still closed. Her house and her devices, however, know she’s awake. Her smart watch detected a switch in her sleep stage from REM to light sleep at 6:37 AM, her heart rate variability shifting toward its morning baseline. The lights in the bedroom begin their slow fade in, timed precisely to her circadian rhythm.

items.description: Could We See the First ‘Flash War’ During the Trump Administration? The danger isn’t rogue AI. items.title: The Other RAG in AI: A Runaway Autonomous Gun (RAG) and Why You Should Care
items.description: A framework for armed autonomous systems that have gone completely sideways Breaking the belt: What happens when the trigger mechanism is made of code instead of metal?
